title: What a release shipped never changes: its templates and the renders built in code
assertion: For every git tag `v<version>` that `packaging` can read, oldest first, every file under `swerepo/templates/` and `tests/released/` at that tag still exists with the same content, as a file of the repository and not a link or reached through a linked folder (new files are fine). Every snapshot in `tests/released/*.json` matches what `rebuild.rebuild` produces today for each template id and inputs it records, whether or not any tag exists. When this SWERepo's own version, as installed or as `pyproject.toml` declares it, is a release, `tests/released/<version>.json` exists and covers every template id put together in code: the `github` builders and every `ci/workflow` and `ci/pyproject` version. A shallow clone fails the rule; a copy of the files without git passes the tag part and warns that it couldn't look.

origin.text: ADR-20261124-41e9 rule 2 and ADR-20261120-b25a (Phase 8, the owner's decision of 2026-11-24): `update` rebuilds earlier renders from the recorded template version, so what a release shipped must never change. Extended by Gemini's design review: renders built in code (P8-D05) and each release's snapshot, required and checked before its tag (P8-D10). Checked by breaking it: a template changed since a tag, a changed ruleset builder against a snapshot, and a release without its snapshot each fail the rule. Refreshed after Gemini's implementation review (P8-F05): the version is also read from pyproject.toml, which a bump changes before `uv sync`, both files are in scope, and a released file replaced by a link counts as changed. Refreshed after SeamSpec's reviewer: a self-check runs the tag comparison on a temporary git repository (a released file changed, deleted or replaced by a link, a new file, a shallow clone, a worktree, no git), so the core of the rule is exercised before the first release; swerepo/render.py is in scope. Refreshed again after SeamSpec's reviewer's second read: the snapshot requirement is self-checked on a temporary folder (missing, incomplete, complete, and ci.released on a release), the no-git warning is exercised, a released file reached through a linked folder counts as changed, and the tag self-check covers tests/released/ too.
